TechnologyStack.Runtime: None required for repository readers or Markdown-only task authoring
TechnologyStack.Language: GitHub Flavored Markdown; embedded JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, and TSX use task-specific versions
TechnologyStack.Framework: GitHub repository rendering; React examples use task-specific versions

dep.name: github-markdown-renderer
dep.purpose: Render README files, relative links, code fences, tables, and collapsed details sections

constraint.reason: Each task must state any language, React, or browser API version assumptions that affect its solution

ContentVocabulary.language-policy: Russian task prose and stable section labels by default; task-specific exceptions require mentor direction.
ContentVocabulary.metadata-labels: Технологии; Тема; Уровень; Время; Навыки; Предварительные знания
ContentVocabulary.technology-policy: Use an existing catalog value such as JavaScript, TypeScript, or React; a new value requires mentor approval.
ContentVocabulary.topic-policy: Use one existing human-readable catalog topic; a new topic requires mentor approval to prevent synonyms.
ContentVocabulary.level-policy: Use one existing catalog level; the initial level vocabulary is established with the first approved task wave.
ContentVocabulary.duration-policy: Use a human-readable estimated duration or range in minutes.
ContentVocabulary.skills-policy: Use a concise list of observable skills exercised by the task.
ContentVocabulary.prerequisites-policy: Use none or relative links to existing task cards plus any concise undeclared external knowledge requirement.

PreferredAgentStack.preferred-content-format: GitHub Flavored Markdown with relative repository links
PreferredAgentStack.preferred-progressive-disclosure: One details block for theory, one per hint, and one for the solution
PreferredAgentStack.preferred-verification: Direct file inspection, stable anchors, link resolution, XML validation, and sampled GitHub rendered-view review
PreferredAgentStack.preferred-grace-resolution: Resolve grace from PATH, then fall back to $HOME/.bun/bin/grace before treating the CLI as unavailable.

discouraged-surface.reason: The initial project intentionally has no repository runtime.

PreferredAgentStack.discouraged-surface: catalog generators, site frameworks, and package-manager-based Markdown pipelines

module-level.command: Use rg and direct reads to verify exact metadata labels, headings, summary anchors, and closed details blocks in the changed document.
module-level.focus: Fast deterministic document-contract checks close to one module.

wave-level.command: Enumerate task cards, compare canonical metadata with README.md catalog entries, and resolve changed relative links against the filesystem.
wave-level.focus: Prove atomic synchronization across task, catalog, and knowledge graph changes.

phase-level.command: Run xmllint on docs/*.xml, scan changed files for whitespace and placeholder defects, review the full catalog projection, and inspect GitHub rendering when template or HTML markup changes.
phase-level.focus: Repository-wide structural integrity and student-visible GitHub behavior.

Testing.mocking-policy: No mocks or fakes; verification uses the actual Markdown and repository paths.

Observability.required-fields: moduleId, verificationRef, artifactPath, checkResult, beadsIssueId, mentorReviewStatus
Observability.stable-anchors: metadata table; Условие; Критерии готовности; Теория; Подсказка N; Решение; Самопроверка
Observability.redaction: Never place secrets, credentials, private student data, or proprietary source material in task cards or evidence.

AutonomyPolicy.replan-trigger: Ambiguous metadata, missing prerequisite or asset, task/catalog contradiction, unexpected GitHub rendering, or a solution requiring undeclared knowledge.
AutonomyPolicy.checkpoint-requirement: Every task change must report assumptions, artifacts changed, checks run, evidence captured, mentor-review status, and next action.

DeliveryShape.shape: GitHub repository whose root README is the student entry point and whose task directories render self-contained Markdown cards.
